title: Zero-Sum Extensions of Zero-Correlation Attacks
summary: Integral distinguishers can often exploit a weaker zero-sum condition, but whether zero-correlation attacks admit an analogous extension remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether zero-correlation attacks can be extended by relaxing their balanced property to a zero-sum property, equivalently to the condition that a certain subfunction does not have maximal algebraic degree. Integral distinguishers often allow this relaxation, but no analogous extension is known for zero-correlation attacks.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis involving integral distinguishers and zero-correlation attacks.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the balanced property in zero-correlation attacks can be relaxed to a zero-sum property, equivalently to a non-maximal algebraic-degree condition on a subfunction.

citations.label: Integral and Multidimensional Linear Distinguishers with Correlation Zero

progress.summary: The source presents this as an unresolved limitation: integral distinguishers often support the relaxation, while no analogous extension was known for zero-correlation attacks.
citation_labels: Andrey Bogdanov et al., Integral and Multidimensional Linear Distinguishers with Correlation Zero
